channelTitle: Two brothers split the harvest in half - then the piles stopped making sense - Part 1
hook: Two brothers split a wheat harvest in half - then each secretly carried sacks to the other's pile at night, for reasons neither would admit.
storyParts: An old folktale tells of two brothers who farmed one field together. Their father had died young and left them only the land - and they worked it side by side for thirty years without a quarrel.
Come harvest, they split the wheat into two equal piles - one beside each brother's house - and went to bed fair and square, the way they always did.
That night, the older brother lay awake. His younger brother had a wife and children to feed, he thought - a sack of wheat means more to a household than to a man alone.
So he shouldered a sack of his own wheat, crept across the dark field, and poured it quietly onto his brother's pile. Then he went home and slept well.
What he didn't know: at that same hour, on the other side of the field, his younger brother was lying awake too - thinking about HIM.
